import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Connect to the SQLite database
conn = sqlite3.connect('data.db')

# Read the data from the table (assuming table name is 'locations')
df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM locations", conn)

# Compute distance matrix via self-join
# First, create a Cartesian product of the table with itself
query = """
SELECT 
    a.id as id1, 
    b.id as id2,
    SQRT(POW(a.x - b.x, 2) + POW(a.y - b.y, 2)) as distance
FROM locations a
CROSS JOIN locations b
WHERE a.id != b.id
ORDER BY a.id, b.id
"""

distance_df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)

# Pivot to create a distance matrix
distance_matrix = distance_df.pivot(index='id1', columns='id2', values='distance')

# Fill diagonal with zeros (distance from a point to itself)
np.fill_diagonal(distance_matrix.values, 0)

# Close the connection
conn.close()

print("Distance matrix computed successfully:")
print(distance_matrix.head())
